title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat in Bhubaneswar or Cuttack, say what is broken, get the landlord to have it fixed, deal with water, power cuts and rubbish, and keep things friendly with the neighbours.
intro:
Live in Bhubaneswar for a few months and it will all happen to you: the geyser packs up, the ceiling starts leaking the week the monsoon arrives, the power goes just as the match starts, and the people upstairs have guests till midnight. This unit gives you the Odia to handle it — the renting words (half of them English with Odia endings), saying exactly what's wrong, asking the landlord to *get it fixed*, and talking to neighbours without starting a feud.

The two skills are **complaining politely but firmly** (ତିନି ଦିନ ହେଲା ପାଣି ଆସୁନି — ଟିକେ ଦେଖିବେ କି?) and **getting something done by someone else**, with the causative verbs in **-ଆଇବା**: ଠିକ୍ **କରାଇଲି** 'I *had* it fixed'.

vocab.en: rented house or flat; a place to rent
vocab.note: ଭଡ଼ା (rent) + ଘର. ଭଡ଼ାରେ ଦେବା / ନେବା = to let / to rent.
With endings: ଫ୍ଲାଟରେ (phlaṭôre), ଫ୍ଲାଟର (phlaṭôrô).
Spoken about in the respectful plural: ଘରମାଲିକ ତଳେ ରହନ୍ତି.
The everyday word in Odisha for the security deposit, usually one to three months' rent.
The formal Odia word is ଚୁକ୍ତି (chukti), used on paper; in speech people say ଏଗ୍ରିମେଣ୍ଟ୍.
ପ୍ରତି ମାସ = every month, a month; ପ୍ରତିଦିନ = every day. Colloquially also ମାସକୁ 'per month'.

vocab.en: uncle (polite way to address an older man)
vocab.note: Literally the husband of your ମାଉସୀ. Used for landlords, neighbours, shopkeepers of your parents' age; the woman is ମାଉସୀ.
ପାଣି କଳ = water tap. Many people just say ଟ୍ୟାପ୍.
ଲିକ୍ ହେବା = to leak: ଛାତରୁ ପାଣି ଲିକ୍ ହେଉଛି.
ଛାତ ଉପରେ = up on the (flat) roof, where the water tank is.
From English 'current'. କରେଣ୍ଟ ଗଲା = there's a power cut; କରେଣ୍ଟ ଆସିଲା = the power's back. The news says ବିଜୁଳି.
Most buildings pump water up to a roof tank: ମୋଟର୍ ଚଲାଅ = switch the pump on.
ଅଳିଆ ଗାଡ଼ି = the municipal garbage van.
The all-purpose word for anyone who comes to fix things.
With endings: ପ୍ଲମ୍ବରକୁ (plômbôrôku).
ପାଇପ୍ ଫାଟିଗଲା = the pipe has burst.
ତାଲା ଲଗାଇବା = to lock up.

vocab.en: to put up, fit, install; to apply
vocab.note: Causative of ଲାଗିବା. Spoken ଲଗେଇବା.
ଘର ବଦଳାଇବା = to move house.
ଆସ୍ତେ କୁହ = speak quietly; ଟିଭି ଆସ୍ତେ କର = turn the TV down.
ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବା = to make a complaint. Colloquially also କମ୍ପ୍ଲେନ୍ କରିବା.
Echo-style pair: ଜିନିଷ + ପତ୍ର.
ସିଫ୍ଟ୍ କରିବା = to move house — far more common in speech than ଘର ବଦଳାଇବା.

How many times have I told you!

Could you turn the TV down a bit? (polite)

grammar.title: Complaining politely but firmly
grammar.body:
A good complaint in Odia has three steps: **say what's wrong**, **ask** (don't order), and if nothing happens, **press the point** — while keeping ଆପଣ and a friendly tone.

**1. What's wrong.** Something going wrong right now takes the continuous: ପାଣି ଲିକ୍ **ହେଉଛି** 'water is leaking'. For 'isn't working / isn't coming', speech uses the short negative **-ଉନି** (= -ଉ ନାହିଁ): ଗିଜର୍ କାମ **କରୁନି**, ପାଣି **ଆସୁନି**, ପଙ୍ଖା **ଚାଲୁନି**, କଳ ବନ୍ଦ **ହେଉନି** 'the tap won't shut'. Something that has broken takes the completed form: ଗିଜର୍ ଖରାପ **ହୋଇଗଲା**.

**How long**: put **(time) ହେଲା** in front — ତିନି ଦିନ **ହେଲା** ପାଣି ଆସୁନି 'there's been no water for three days', literally 'three days have gone by, water isn't coming'. Odia keeps the present (ଆସୁନି) where English says 'hasn't come'. Ask it with କେତେ ଦିନ ହେଲା …?

**2. The request.** Ask with the polite future + **କି**: **ଟିକେ ଦେଖିବେ କି?** 'could you take a look?'. Add the favour-helper **ଦେବା** (unit 18): ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ **ପଠାଇଦେବେ?** 'would you send someone?'. Soften with **ଟିକେ**, **ଦୟାକରି**, and the address **ମଉସା / ମାଉସୀ**.

**3. Pressing the point.** The **'already' perfect in -ଲିଣି** adds impatience: ମୁଁ ତିନି ଥର **କହିଲିଣି** 'I've told you three times already'. Its forms: ମୁଁ କହିଲିଣି · ତୁମେ କହିଲଣି · ସେ କହିଲାଣି · ଆମେ କହିଲୁଣି · ଆପଣ / ସେମାନେ କହିଲେଣି. Add **ବାରମ୍ବାର** 'again and again', **ଆଜି ହିଁ** 'today itself', and the last resort with **ନହେଲେ**: ନହେଲେ ମୋତେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ 'otherwise I'll have to complain'.

The trap: a bare command like **ଠିକ୍ କରନ୍ତୁ!** to your landlord sounds like an order, even with -ନ୍ତୁ. Describe the problem and ask a question (**ଦେଖିବେ କି?**) — let them offer.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: getting things done around the house
grammar.body:
You met the causative **-ଆଇବା** in the errands unit (ଠିକ୍ କରାଇବା, ଧୁଆଇବା). Around the house it's everywhere, and a few more pairs are worth knowing:

ଲାଗିବା 'be attached, stick' → **ଲଗାଇବା** 'put up, fit, install'
ଚାଲିବା 'go, run' → **ଚଲାଇବା** 'switch on, run (a machine)'
ଫେରିବା 'come back' → **ଫେରାଇବା** 'give back, return'
ବଦଳିବା 'change' → **ବଦଳାଇବା** 'replace, change (something)'
ଠିକ୍ ହେବା 'get fixed' → ଠିକ୍ କରିବା 'fix' → **ଠିକ୍ କରାଇବା** 'have fixed'

They take the ordinary endings: ଘରମାଲିକ ନୂଆ ଗିଜର୍ **ଲଗାଇବେ** 'the landlord will put in a new geyser', ଆଡଭାନ୍ସ **ଫେରାଇଦେବେ** 'they'll give the deposit back'. In fast speech -ଆଇ- sounds **-ଏଇ-** (କରେଇଲି, ଲଗେଇବେ) — say it that way, but it's written with ଆ.

**Bringing in the worker**: the most natural tenant's sentence uses the 'do and then' participle — ପ୍ଲମ୍ବରକୁ **ଡାକି** କଳ ଠିକ୍ କରାଇଲି 'I called the plumber and had the tap fixed'. (At a shop you'd use ପାଖରେ: ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ପାଖରେ ଠିକ୍ କରାଇଲି.)

**Who arranges it** is the real question between tenant and landlord:
- 'I need to get … done': ମୋତେ … **କରାଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ**.
- Asking the landlord to arrange it: add ଦେବା — ଛାତ ମରାମତି **କରାଇଦିଅନ୍ତୁ** 'please have the roof repaired (for us)', ଆଲୁଅ **ଲଗାଇଦେବେ?**
- The landlord promising: ମୁଁ **କରାଇଦେବି** 'I'll get it done for you'.

The trap: **କରିଦେବି** 'I'll do it (for you) myself' vs **କରାଇଦେବି** 'I'll have someone do it'. When the landlord says ମୁଁ କରାଇଦେବି, he's calling a ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ — and paying.

examples.en: The landlord will put in a new geyser.
We called the plumber and had the tap fixed.
You'll return the deposit when we leave, won't you?
I'll have to get the geyser fixed.
Uncle, please get the roof repaired.

dialogue.title: A word with the landlord
dialogue.setting: Saheed Nagar, Bhubaneswar, in the first week of the monsoon. Ankit rents the upstairs flat and goes down to see his landlord, Mishra-uncle, who lives on the ground floor.

lines.speaker: Ankit
lines.native: ନମସ୍କାର ମଉସା, ଟିକେ ସମୟ ଅଛି କି?
lines.roman: nômôskarô môusa, ṭike sômôyô ôchhi ki?
lines.en: Hello uncle — have you got a minute?

lines.speaker: Ankit
lines.native: ଛାତରୁ ପାଣି ଲିକ୍ ହେଉଛି। କାଲି ରାତିରେ ମୋ ଖଟ ପୂରା ଓଦା ହୋଇଗଲା।
lines.roman: chhatôru paṇi lik heuchhi. kali ratire mo khôṭô pura oda hoigôla.
lines.en: The ceiling's leaking. Last night my bed got completely soaked.

lines.speaker: Mishra
lines.en: Oh my! And the monsoon's already here.

lines.speaker: Ankit
lines.native: ଆଉ ଗିଜର୍ ବି ଏକ ସପ୍ତାହ ହେଲା କାମ କରୁନି। ମୁଁ ଦୁଇ ଥର ଫୋନରେ କହିଥିଲି।
lines.roman: au gijôr bi ekô sôptahô hela kamô kôruni. muṃ dui thôrô phonôre kôhithili.
lines.en: And the geyser hasn't worked for a week either. I told you twice on the phone.

lines.speaker: Mishra
lines.native: ହଁ ହଁ, ମନେ ଅଛି। ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଆସିବାର କଥା ଥିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେ ଆସିଲା ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: hôṃ hôṃ, mône ôchhi. mistri asibarô kôtha thila, kintu se asila nahiṃ.
lines.en: Yes, yes, I remember. The repairman was supposed to come, but he never showed up.

lines.speaker: Ankit
lines.native: ମଉସା, ଆଜି ହିଁ କାହାକୁ ପଠାଇଦେବେ କି? ଥଣ୍ଡା ପାଣିରେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଗାଧୋଇ ମୋର ସର୍ଦ୍ଦି ହୋଇଗଲାଣି।
lines.roman: môusa, aji hiṃ kahaku pôṭhaidebe ki? thôṇḍa paṇire gadhoi gadhoi morô sôrddi hoigôlaṇi.
lines.en: Uncle, could you send someone today? With all these cold showers I've caught a cold.

lines.speaker: Mishra
lines.native: ହା ହା, ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି। ମୁଁ ଏବେ ହିଁ ପ୍ଲମ୍ବରକୁ ଫୋନ କରୁଛି। ଛାତ ବି ମରାମତି କରାଇଦେବି।
lines.roman: ha ha, ṭhik ôchhi. muṃ ebe hiṃ plômbôrôku phonô kôruchhi. chhatô bi môramôti kôraidebi.
lines.en: Ha ha, all right. I'm calling the plumber right now. And I'll get the roof repaired too.

lines.speaker: Ankit
lines.native: ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ ମଉସା। ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ କଥା… ଉପର ଫ୍ଲାଟରୁ ରାତି ବାରଟା ଯାଏ ବହୁତ ଶବ୍ଦ ଆସେ।

lines.en: Thanks, uncle. One more thing… there's a lot of noise from the flat above until midnight.

lines.speaker: Mishra
lines.native: ଓହୋ, ସେମାନେ ନୂଆ ଆସିଛନ୍ତି। ପିଲାମାନେ ଭଲ, ମୁଁ ଟିକେ କହିଦେବି।
lines.roman: oho, semane nua asichhônti. pilamane bhôlô, muṃ ṭike kôhidebi.
lines.en: Oh, they've just moved in. They're nice kids — I'll have a word.

lines.speaker: Ankit
lines.native: ନା ନା, ମୁଁ ନିଜେ କହିବି। ଝଗଡ଼ା କରିବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁନି, ଖାଲି ଟିକେ ଆସ୍ତେ।
lines.roman: na na, muṃ nije kôhibi. jhôgôṛa kôribaku chahuṃni, khali ṭike aste.
lines.en: No, no, I'll tell them myself. I don't want a fight — just a bit quieter.

lines.speaker: Mishra
lines.native: ହଉ, ସେଇଟା ଭଲ। ଆଉ ଶୁଣ, ଏ ମାସର କରେଣ୍ଟ ବିଲ୍ ଆସିଗଲାଣି, ମୁଁ ୱାଟ୍ସଆପ୍ କରିଦେବି।
lines.roman: hôu, seiṭa bhôlô. au suṇô, e masôrô kôreṇṭ bil asigôlaṇi, muṃ waṭsap kôridebi.
lines.en: Fine, that's better. Oh, and listen — this month's electricity bill has come; I'll WhatsApp it to you.

culture:
In Bhubaneswar and Cuttack a lot of renting happens inside family houses: the owner lives on the ground floor and lets the floor above, so your landlord is also your neighbour. You call him **ମଉସା** and her **ମାଉସୀ**, use **ଆପଣ**, and they will probably call you **ତୁମେ** and ask where your family is from and whether you're married. Landlords often prefer families to 'bachelors'; students and young professionals tend to end up in newer flats in Patia, Chandrasekharpur or near the IT parks. Expect an **ଆଡଭାନ୍ସ** of one to three months' rent and an 11-month **ଏଗ୍ରିମେଣ୍ଟ୍**; the electricity bill (the **କରେଣ୍ଟ ବିଲ୍**) is usually separate.

Everyday life has its own vocabulary. Water is pumped up to a tank on the roof, so 'switch on the motor' (**ମୋଟର୍ ଚଲାଅ**) is a daily phrase. In summer storms and cyclones the power goes often — **କରେଣ୍ଟ ଗଲା!** is shouted across many households at once, and **କରେଣ୍ଟ ଆସିଲା!** is cheered. The municipal garbage van announces itself with music or a whistle early in the morning. Mosquitoes are serious business in the monsoon: nets (**ମଶାରି**), coils and repellents are in every home.

With neighbours, keep complaints soft and indirect: **ଟିକେ ଆସ୍ତେ କରିବେ?** works far better than a demand. Neighbours share food at festivals — at **Raja** in June you may well get a plate of *poda pitha* — and it's polite to return the plate with something on it.

lessons.title: Looking for a flat to rent

tip.title: Renting talk: English words, Odia endings
tip.body:
- Many renting words are English: **ଫ୍ଲାଟ୍, ଆଡଭାନ୍ସ, ଏଗ୍ରିମେଣ୍ଟ୍** — Odia adds the endings: ଫ୍ଲାଟ**ର** ଭଡ଼ା, ଫ୍ଲାଟ**କୁ**.
- 'Per month': **ପ୍ରତି ମାସ**; 'two months' rent': ଦୁଇ ମାସ**ର** ଭଡ଼ା.
- Speak to the landlord with **ଆପଣ**, and about them in the respectful plural: ଘରମାଲିକ **ରହନ୍ତି**.

tip.title: ଚାଲୁନି, ଆସୁନି — what's wrong and since when
tip.body:
- Happening now: ପାଣି ଲିକ୍ **ହେଉଛି**.
- Isn't working: spoken **-ଉନି** (= -ଉ ନାହିଁ): ଗିଜର୍ କାମ **କରୁନି**, ପାଣି **ଆସୁନି**.
- Has broken: ଖରାପ **ହୋଇଗଲା**.
- For how long: **(time) ହେଲା** first — ତିନି ଦିନ **ହେଲା** ପାଣି ଆସୁନି.

lessons.title: Getting the landlord to fix it

tip.title: Ask, then press: ଦେଖିବେ କି? · କହିଲିଣି
tip.body:
- Ask, don't order: **ଟିକେ ଦେଖିବେ କି?** · ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ **ପଠାଇଦେବେ?**
- Fed up? The 'already' ending **-ଲିଣି**: ମୁଁ ତିନି ଥର **କହିଲିଣି** (ତୁମେ କହିଲଣି, ସେ କହିଲାଣି, ଆପଣ କହିଲେଣି).
- Last resort: **ନହେଲେ** ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ 'otherwise I'll have to complain'.

sentences.en: Uncle, could you take a look at the geyser?
Could you send a plumber today?
I've told you again and again.

sentences.native: ତୁମେ ତାକୁ କେତେ ଥର ଫୋନ କଲଣି?
sentences.roman: tume taku kete thôrô phonô kôlôṇi?
sentences.en: How many times have you phoned him already?

sentences.native: ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଆସିବ ବୋଲି କହିଥିଲେ, କିନ୍ତୁ କେହି ଆସିଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: mistri asibô boli kôhithile, kintu kehi asila nahiṃ.
sentences.en: You said a repairman would come, but nobody came.

sentences.native: ଦୟାକରି ଆଜି ହିଁ ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ, ନହେଲେ ମୋତେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
sentences.roman: dôyakôri aji hiṃ dekhôntu, nôhele mote ôbhijogô kôribaku pôṛibô.
sentences.en: Please look at it today, otherwise I'll have to complain.
When will the plumber come?
The repairman has just got here.

sentences.native: ମଉସା, ମୁଁ ରାଗୁନି, କିନ୍ତୁ ବହୁତ ଅସୁବିଧା ହେଉଛି।
sentences.roman: môusa, muṃ raguni, kintu bôhutô ôsubidha heuchhi.
sentences.en: Uncle, I'm not angry, but it's really causing problems.

tip.title: Power cuts and pumps
tip.body:
- **କରେଣ୍ଟ ଗଲା / ଚାଲିଗଲା** = the power's gone; **କରେଣ୍ଟ ଆସିଲା** = it's back.
- Water is pumped to a roof tank: **ମୋଟର୍ ଚଲାଅ** 'switch the pump on', ମୋଟର୍ **ବନ୍ଦ କର** 'switch it off'.
- 'When the power comes': **-ଲେ** form — କରେଣ୍ଟ **ଆସିଲେ**.

sentences.en: The power's gone again!
When the power comes back I'll switch the pump on.
There's no water in the tank — switch the pump on.
The tank's full now — switch the pump off.

sentences.native: କରେଣ୍ଟ ଗଲେ ଗିଜର୍ ବି ଚାଲେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: kôreṇṭ gôle gijôr bi chale nahiṃ.
sentences.en: When the power goes, the geyser doesn't work either.

sentences.native: ଏ ମାସର କରେଣ୍ଟ ବିଲ୍ କେତେ ଆସିଲା?
sentences.roman: e masôrô kôreṇṭ bil kete asila?
sentences.en: How much did this month's electricity bill come to?
The garbage van comes at seven in the morning.
Please don't leave rubbish here.

sentences.native: ଏଠି ବହୁତ ମଶା, ଝରକା ବନ୍ଦ କର।
sentences.roman: eṭhi bôhutô môsa, jhôrôka bôndô kôrô.
sentences.en: There are loads of mosquitoes here — shut the window.

tip.title: Getting it done around the house
tip.body:
- More causatives: ଲାଗିବା → **ଲଗାଇବା** 'install', ଫେରିବା → **ଫେରାଇବା** 'return', ଚାଲିବା → **ଚଲାଇବା** 'switch on'.
- ଠିକ୍ **କଲି** = I fixed it; ଠିକ୍ **କରାଇଲି** = I had it fixed.
- Bring in the worker with **ଡାକି**: ପ୍ଲମ୍ବରକୁ ଡାକି …
- Need to: **କରାଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ**; ask the landlord: **କରାଇଦିଅନ୍ତୁ**.

sentences.en: I got the geyser fixed yesterday.
The landlord will put in a new tap.
We got the plumber in and had the bathroom tap replaced.
I'll have to get the roof repaired.
Uncle, could you have a light put up on the veranda?

sentences.native: ପଙ୍ଖା ମୁଁ ହିଁ ଠିକ୍ କଲି, ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଦରକାର ହେଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: pôṅkha muṃ hiṃ ṭhik kôli, mistri dôrôkarô hela nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I fixed the fan myself — didn't need a repairman.

sentences.native: ଦୁଆରର ତାଲା ଭଙ୍ଗା, ନୂଆ ତାଲା ଲଗାଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
sentences.roman: duarôrô tala bhôṅga, nua tala lôgaibaku pôṛibô.
sentences.en: The door lock's broken — we'll have to put on a new one.

sentences.native: ରୋଷେଇ ଘରର ପାଇପ୍ ଲିକ୍ ହେଉଛି, ମିସ୍ତ୍ରୀକୁ ଡାକି ବଦଳାଇଦେବି।
sentences.roman: rosei ghôrôrô paip lik heuchhi, mistriku ḍaki bôdôḷaidebi.
sentences.en: The kitchen pipe is leaking — I'll get a repairman in and have it replaced.
Tell the landlord and get the door fixed.

tip.title: Neighbours: soft, indirect, friendly
tip.body:
- Older neighbours are **ମଉସା / ମାଉସୀ**, people your age **ଭାଇନା / ଅପା** — with ଆପଣ until they say otherwise.
- Make a complaint a question: ଟିଭି ଟିକେ **ଆସ୍ତେ କରିବେ?**
- If it was you: **ମାଫ କରିବେ** + the reason.
- Moving house is **ସିଫ୍ଟ୍ କରିବା** in everyday speech.

sentences.en: Our neighbours are really nice people.

sentences.native: ଉପର ଫ୍ଲାଟରୁ ରାତିରେ ବହୁତ ଶବ୍ଦ ଆସେ।
sentences.roman: upôrô phlaṭôru ratire bôhutô sôbdô ase.
sentences.en: There's a lot of noise from the flat upstairs at night.
Could you turn the music down a little?

sentences.native: ମାଉସୀ, ମାଫ କରିବେ, କାଲି ଆମ ଘରେ ସାଙ୍ଗମାନେ ଥିଲେ।
sentences.roman: mausi, maphô kôribe, kali amô ghôre saṅgômane thile.
sentences.en: Sorry, auntie — we had friends over yesterday.
Talk quietly, the baby's asleep.

sentences.native: ଆମେ ଶନିବାର ନୂଆ ଫ୍ଲାଟକୁ ସିଫ୍ଟ୍ କରିବା।
sentences.roman: ame sônibarô nua phlaṭôku siphṭ kôriba.
sentences.en: We're moving to the new flat on Saturday.

sentences.native: ଜିନିଷପତ୍ର ବହୁତ, ଗୋଟିଏ ବଡ଼ ଗାଡ଼ି ଦରକାର।
sentences.roman: jinisôpôtrô bôhutô, goṭie bôṛô gaṛi dôrôkarô.
sentences.en: There's loads of stuff — we need a big vehicle.
The landlord will give the deposit back, won't they?

sentences.native: ଯିବା ଆଗରୁ ତାଲା ଲଗାଇ ପଡ଼ୋଶୀଙ୍କୁ ଚାବି ଦେଇଯାଅ।
sentences.roman: jiba agôru tala lôgai pôṛosiṅku chabi deijaô.
sentences.en: Before you go, lock up and leave the key with the neighbours.
